compiled_state.title: Migrate CI LLM review runner from bash to Python module + LiteLLM provider abstraction (Anthropic + OpenAI)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

The CI LLM review runner (`ci-llm-review-runner.sh` plus `llm-api-call.sh`) is bash + 5+ inline `python3` heredocs with regex-fallback JSON parsing, three near-identical curl blocks for specialists + a fourth for arch synthesis. Adding a third provider is O(N) shell complexity — each new provider requires a new bash branch, a new heredoc, and a new response-extraction regex. Unit testing requires `PATH`-mocked curl driving the whole script; there are no unit-testable functions. This epic migrates orchestration to a Python package (`plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/`) and adopts LiteLLM as the provider abstraction. Anthropic and OpenAI both ship in this epic. Tool-use loop, prompt caching, and exhaustion handling follow in a downstream epic; Gemini follows in a placeholder follow-on epic. Both downstream epics are blocked by this one. Doing the migration in isolation produces a stable Python foundation for those downstream epics to land on, and a single parity-test cycle to validate that schema and behavior are preserved across the cutover.

## Success Criteria

- New `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration. Modules: `runner.py` (entry-point), `classifier.py` (tier selection — pure function), `dispatch.py` (`asyncio.gather` for parallel specialists + overlay calls), `providers/` (LiteLLM-backed clients behind a common interface), `findings.py` (single JSON normalization implementation replacing the 5+ inline heredocs). `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` reduced to ≤50 lines and exists only as a thin shim that resolves `_PLUGIN_ROOT` and execs `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`. `llm-api-call.sh` deleted. References in `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`, `ci-overlay-flags.md`, and `onboarding/SKILL.md` updated to reflect the new module layout.
- LiteLLM-backed provider abstraction: Anthropic and OpenAI both functional in CI runs, verified by an integration test exercising each provider end-to-end against fixture diffs. LiteLLM is pinned to an **exact** version (`litellm==<version>`) in the package's lockfile — compatible-release (`~=`) and range pinning (`>=`) are explicitly rejected by a CI lint step that scans the lockfile, to remain immune to the supply-chain attack class confirmed in March 2026 (versions 1.82.7 / 1.82.8). A parity-test gate is required before any LiteLLM version bump is accepted. Adding the Gemini follow-on epic requires only a new entry under `providers/` plus a config key — no changes to `runner.py`, `dispatch.py`, or `findings.py`. Verified by adding a stub `mock` provider in tests as the third implementation.
- Schema-equivalent `reviewer-findings.json` parity across the fixture corpus: same fixture diffs produce findings JSON that conforms to the existing schema and preserves the full set of pre-migration `critical` / `important` / `fragile` findings (additive findings allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped). The parity test additionally asserts **zero dropped findings** relative to the pre-migration baseline on the fixture corpus — eliminating the silent-drop failure mode of the current bash regex-fallback JSON parsing. Parity-test job runs in CI for the duration of the epic and is removed at epic close. Pre-migration baseline captured as a checked-in golden corpus in story 1, before migration begins, and reused by the downstream tool-use epic's before/after grounded-finding comparison.
- `asyncio.gather` partial-failure handling produces a user-observable improvement vs. the current bash behavior: when one specialist or overlay provider call fails (5xx-class error, network failure, timeout), the review degrades to partial findings instead of aborting the whole run, and the engineer sees an explicit error entry for the failed specialist on the PR (current bash runner aborts the entire review on a single error). Verified by a test that injects a 5xx-class error into one specialist call and asserts the resulting `reviewer-findings.json` includes (a) the surviving specialists' findings and (b) an explicit error entry for the failed specialist that surfaces in the PR review summary.
- Per-module unit tests using `respx` / `httpx.MockTransport`-style provider mocks (no `PATH`-mocked curl in unit tests). Integration tests exercise both Anthropic and OpenAI end-to-end. **Story 1 transport-verification acceptance criterion**: instantiate a LiteLLM client in the same configuration `providers/` will use and assert its internal HTTP transport is `httpx`-based for the Anthropic and OpenAI provider paths. If `aiohttp` is detected on any path, **substitute `pytest-httpx` for `respx`** as the test mock — do not rely on `DISABLE_AIOHTTP_TRANSPORT` or the `httpx_client` parameter as a forcing mechanism, as both have open reliability bugs across providers (LiteLLM #12581, #13049). Document the detected transport per provider before any provider unit tests are written. CI install pipeline uses `actions/setup-python` (or platform equivalent) with `cache: 'pip'` against a checked-in lockfile so cold-runner pip install does not regress CI run duration. **CI run duration neutral-or-better**: post-migration p50 and p95 CI review-job duration on the fixture corpus is no greater than the bash-baseline duration captured before migration begins; verified by comparison script at epic close. All existing CI invocation surfaces (`ci-llm-review-runner.sh` shim, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `templates/ci-dso-staged.yml`, `tests/scripts/test-ci-llm-review-job.sh`, `test-ci-llm-review-runner.sh`) continue to work without per-platform conditionals.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: reviewer-findings.json schema and CI / local review parity
  Interaction: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema) removes the scores object and `REVIEW_RESULT` / `MIN_SCORE` lines; this epic's `findings.py` is where the CI half of that schema change must propagate. This epic blocks 4b8f-924d.
  Gate: schema collision resolved via the `blocks` dependency + 4b8f-924d's description has been updated to apply the schema removal across both the CI path (post-this-epic) and the local `/dso:review` path.
- Resource: ci-llm-review-runner.sh shim invocation surface
  Interaction: 1083-fb3d (Local workflow simplification → enforcement.strategy=ci) flips strategy and exercises the shim invocation surface; this epic reduces the shim to ≤50 lines while preserving the invocation surface byte-for-byte.
  Gate: 1083-fb3d's PR-mode integration test must verify the new shim correctly dispatches to the `dso_ci_review` module.
- Resource: REVIEW-DEFENSE comments in CI review scripts
  Interaction: 5018-64ce (Evaluate REVIEW-DEFENSE comments) audits review-defense annotations including those in `ci-llm-review-runner.sh`; this epic rewrites those scripts.
  Gate: coordinate timing — either 5018-64ce captures defenses pre-rewrite, or this epic ensures defenses migrate into the Python module as needed.
- Resource: tool-use authorization layer (separate from runtime adapter)
  Interaction: 2239-1545 (Cross-runtime support via harness adapter) addresses AI tool runtime event normalization (Claude Code vs. Cursor vs. OpenCode vs. Codex hook stdin); this epic's LiteLLM provider abstraction is at the LLM API layer, not the runtime layer. They do not share infrastructure; 2239-1545 remains an open, distinct epic.
  Gate: documented distinction; 2239-1545 stays open.

## Scenario Analysis

- Shim ↔ Python entry-point PATH / venv mismatch in CI (high, deployment): the shim invokes `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`; CI runners may have multiple python3s and the package may not be importable from the shell's `python3` unless installed or path-injected. Mitigation: the shim resolves the package path explicitly and the CI install step uses `actions/setup-python` with cached pip and an editable install (`pip install -e .`) before the runner is invoked.
- llm-api-call.sh deletion breaks out-of-tree consumers (high, deployment): host projects calling the deleted script break without a deprecation window. Mitigation: deprecation announcement in release notes; consider a thin compatibility wrapper in the shim that warns and forwards to the Python entry-point for one minor version.
- LiteLLM version drift breaks tool-use schema (high, runtime): LiteLLM's mapping for tool / response shapes has changed across minor versions and the parallel-tool-use translation has documented production issues (LiteLLM #26529, discussion #18271). Mitigation: pin LiteLLM to a tested minor version in the package lockfile; require a parity-test pass before accepting any LiteLLM version bump; add a renovate / dependabot policy enforcing that gate.
- asyncio.gather partial-failure swallows specialist exceptions (high, runtime): without `return_exceptions=True` and per-task error capture, one transient provider error aborts the whole review. Mitigation: SC4 explicit partial-failure handling.
- Findings parity test masks semantic regressions (high, runtime): shape-only parity passes despite severity downgrades or critical findings dropped. Mitigation: SC3 parity test compares both schema conformance and preservation of every pre-migration critical / important / fragile finding by id / title; additive findings are allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped.
- Provider auth secrets not provisioned for OpenAI path on day one (high, deployment): rollout requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` in org / repo secrets before merge. Mitigation: secrets-provisioning step is part of the rollout plan and listed as a story precondition.
- Provider routing config has no fail-safe default (medium, configuration): missing or malformed `providers/` config silently switches model. Mitigation: missing config refuses to run with a clear error; default is fail-loud rather than fall back to a provider that may not be authorized.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: 5d6e-86a9 (CI LLM-review parity port — must be fully merged to main before this epic starts).
- Blocks: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema removal must propagate through the new `findings.py`).
- Blocks: tool-use + caching downstream epic (operates on this epic's merged Python module + LiteLLM abstraction).
- Blocks: Gemini placeholder follow-on epic (Gemini provider entry depends on this epic's LiteLLM provider abstraction).

## Research Findings

- External Integration: LiteLLM provider abstraction — Parallel tool calls supported across Anthropic + OpenAI via OpenAI-format function-calling schema; passthrough adapter active. Key insight: LiteLLM as provider router is well-supported, but minor-version pinning is required because the Anthropic / OpenAI tool-use translation has changed across releases (issues #26529, #18271). Sources: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/anthropic , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26529 .
- Performance: LiteLLM caching translation — Auto-injection supported for Anthropic; OpenAI prefix caching is automatic. Known LiteLLM bug on Gemini multi-cache mapping (issue #17201). Key insight: confirms Gemini deferral; Anthropic + OpenAI caching is unaffected and will land in the downstream tool-use + caching epic. Source: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/17201 .
- Operational: CI dependency caching — `actions/setup-python` with `cache: 'pip'` reduces cold pip install from 60–90s to ~2–5s with a checked-in lockfile; `uv` brings sub-second installs. Key insight: cold-install cost is a solved problem in CI; mitigation is SC5 cached install pipeline.

## Approach

Single-epic cutover: a new `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration in one merge with a parity-test gate that runs for the duration of the epic and is removed at epic close. LiteLLM provides the provider abstraction; Anthropic and OpenAI both wired in this epic. Tool-use, prompt caching, and exhaustion handling deliberately deferred to Epic B+C (blocked by this one) so this epic is a pure substrate refactor with a clean parity gate.

### Planning Intelligence Log

- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
  - Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (LiteLLM new dep), novel architectural pattern (Python module replacing bash orchestration), performance (prompt caching considerations carried into Epic B+C)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
  - Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 15 across original folded epic; 7 redistributed to Epic A
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: triggered — depth: 0 (Epic B+C and Gemini placeholder)
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: triggered — cycles: 1, gap: aiohttp-vs-httpx transport ambiguity in LiteLLM Router (#12581) plus exact-version pinning posture for supply-chain attack class (LiteLLM 1.82.7/1.82.8 March 2026); resolved by SC2 (==-pinning + lint) and SC5 (Story 1 transport-verification gate)
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered (substrate refactor; reviewer agent prompts not modified by this epic)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default — bounded fixture corpus; CI run volume governed by PR throughput, not user-traffic scale)
